<hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h1 class="c10 c24" id="h.i7ckpnxrpo8j">
 <span class="c13">
  Introduction
 </span>
</h1>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  We are currently experiencing the convergence of multiple scientific trends that will enable us humans will gain full control over evolution:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_oy88jis9odyu-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   CRISPR
  </span>
  <span class="c2">
   allows us humans to modify our own DNA,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   The internet augments the human memory to the entire sum of human
  </span>
  <span class="c25">
   memory
  </span>
  <span class="c2">
   ,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   AI will allow humans to process inordinate amounts of information thus increasing the scope of our
  </span>
  <span class="c25">
   intuition
  </span>
  <span class="c2">
   ,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   AR allows humans to foundationally improve our field of visual perception and the amount of useful information we can ingest.
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  For the first time in our six million year history (since diverging from our nearest living evolutionary), we will soon be able to control our genetics and augment the cortex that allowed us to become the dominant creatures on Earth.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c25">
  Symbiotic AI
 </span>
 <span>
  expresses the principle that machine agents and human agents can compensate each others’ deficiencies and augment each others’ strengths: Humans have excellent intuition and terrible memory, both honed by millions of years of evolution. Computers have
 </span>
 <span class="c25">
  perfect
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  memory and terrible intuition, both being developed rapidly by increasing computing power although AI is still far from it’s telos of General Intelligence.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Human-machine symbiosis can take many forms:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_ri8stjij20wk-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   a 12 year old spending the entire day with her smartphone being able to research any fact from all of human knowledge after just a few taps, or
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   a student using a Remembrance Agent
  </span>
  <span class="c6">
   <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/0nl3&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479611000">
    [Rhodes 1997]
   </a>
  </span>
  <span class="c2">
   to automatically pull up meeting notes with every person he’s ever met, or
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   a “Borg” like creature (see
  </span>
  <span class="c25">
   Star Trek: Voyager
  </span>
  <span class="c2">
   ) merging man and metal into one being inseparable from each other.
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<a id="t.2d1eb33bf6a9d7e710f1ba79b76acf33a106978e">
</a>
<a id="t.1">
</a>
<table class="c4">
 <tbody>
  <tr class="c14">
   <td class="c39" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <p class="c29 c54">
     <span class="c2">
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
   <td class="c39" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <p class="c40 c29">
     <span class="c2">
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
   <td class="c39" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <p class="c40">
     <span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 194.00px; height: 109.33px;">
      <img alt="" src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 194.00px; height: 109.33px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""/>
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
  </tr>
  <tr class="c14">
   <td class="c39" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <p class="c40 c29">
     <span class="c2">
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
   <td class="c39" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <p class="c29 c40">
     <span class="c2">
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
   <td class="c39" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <p class="c40">
     <span class="c25">
      Seven of Nine
     </span>
     <span>
      from
     </span>
     <span class="c25">
      Star Trek: Voyager
     </span>
     <span class="c6 c25">
      <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/cNpY&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479613000">
       [Fleenor 2019]
      </a>
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  In this text, we primarily investigate non-invasive forms of human augmentation that offer many benefits (explored in depth later) including the option of “turning off” the system and removing wearable augmentations with ease and the acceptability of wearable computers over implanted devices.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  These technologies take the form of wearable computers seen in form factors like watches, HWDs, and smartphones. AR will be investigated as the primary “bridge” between humans and machines, although non-visual alternatives will be explored in depth later.
 </span>
</p>
<hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h1 class="c10 c24" id="h.bsvxru72goy5">
 <span class="c13">
  Human-Machine Symbiosis
 </span>
</h1>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.gb77wrsi9vy8">
 <span>
  Closing the loop between
 </span>
 <span class="c25">
  intention
 </span>
 <span>
  and
 </span>
 <span class="c33 c25 c28 c36">
  action
 </span>
</h2>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Say I want to buy a new car. Which path is easier for me?
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c55 c33 c52">
  Buying a car from a dealership
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_29qu32m9wadk-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I put on shoes,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I go to my existing car (or call a friend to give me a ride)
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I go to a dealership
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I look at the available cars,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I talk to the dealer to buy the car,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I negotiate a price with the dealer,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I talk through all the additional details,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I pay for the car,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I drive away with my new car on that day.
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c33 c52 c55">
  Buying a car online.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_4pzfoz505j40-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I grab my laptop,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I go to tesla.com,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I find the car I want,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I read about and configure all my extras,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I pay for the car,
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   I have the car delivered to me within a week.
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  My intention is the same. However, the two action paths are different: One is rather time and labor intensive (I have to put on shoes!) and the other I can do from my bed. This is the whole premise behind online shopping, more specifically Amazon’s patented 1-Click
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/jiKd&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479617000">
   [Hartman et al. 1999]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  . By reducing the time between intention and action habit can be formed. Once a habit is formed, it’s ingrained, it’s useful, and it’s profitable (for those of that persuasion).
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c25">
  The distance between action and intent
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  : It’s a key concept for the melding of men and machines, humans and AI. Reduce the overhead of a communication bridge or the time to act on a thought and habits are formed, we get closer to our goals and the machine gets closer to us.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.mnzj5s7e0o0v">
 <span class="c1">
  Notes from Pattie Maes: “Human-Machine Symbiosis”
 </span>
</h2>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/se69&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479617000">
   [Maes 1997]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  observes that we’ve experienced a revolution in computing in the past 30 years: our bodies have been augmented in a significant and permanent way; the two “halves” of our brains are no longer the “left” or “right” but instead the biological we are given and the digital we use to voluntarily augment our memory and communication.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  The interface between our biological and digital worlds is currently limited to smartphones and laptops. These modalities are limited by three fundamental problems:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_u9o1ztq11z3p-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   I/O bandwidth is limited.
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Requires our complete attention disengaging us from the physical world.
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   Isn’t designed for the goals of people in mind.
   <br/>
   Different apps on phone are designed to distract you as much as possible, making you as inefficient and ineffective in accomplishing goals leading to increased “multitasking” which contributes to shorter attention spans and worse memory recall
  </span>
  <span class="c6">
   <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/HdB0&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479618000">
    [Stanford University 2018]
   </a>
  </span>
  <span class="c2">
   .
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/se69&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479619000">
   [Maes 1997]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  continues to argue that it is our destiny to augment ourselves with whatever tools and technologies are available and merge with technology itself.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/se69&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479619000">
   [Maes 1997]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  argues that we will become one with the computer, but we must redesign the experience of how someone interacts with their digital devices. In this direction, Maes argues for a new approach built upon three pillars:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_8v2rpwsj10kq-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   A system aware of context and a user’s internal state. It pays attention to what the user is paying attention to, to brain activity, heart rate, breathing rate, etc.
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   An always-on augmented interface integrated in a seamless and non-disruptive way
  </span>
  <sup>
   <a href="#ftnt1" id="ftnt_ref1">
    [1]
   </a>
  </sup>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Roots in proactive and personalized interaction that offers relevant information and intervention, given what the user is currently trying to do, the user’s state, and the user’s real/human goals.
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  In this direction, a symbiotic relationship between users and machines will help with self-actualization itself. It will aid us in growing and developing into the people we want to become: We all want to change and grow in different ways; we will rely on symbiotic forms of personal devices more and more to help us change with time.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Maes outlines four broad categories in how symbiotic systems can support humans:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_wfncvagsog87-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Supporting Decision Making
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Supporting Learning
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Supporting Memory
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Supporting Mood and Well-being
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.h8xdg7b8jd9g">
 <span class="c18">
  Supporting Decision Making
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Up to 90% of the decisions we make are a result of natural thinking that may not be in\line with our goals
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.j8wbweiywh4y">
 <span class="c18">
  Support Learning
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Using AR to label objects in the real world (WordSense). Can give you new words for known objects, etc. Not all of the devices need to rely on a smart AI system
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Google Glass in a supermarket for learning a new language through a “remote assistant” system
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  AR for “remote assistant”
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.v97ybfx78bry">
 <span class="c18">
  Supporting Memory
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Shaking hand to remember someone’s name and face (TakeTwo)
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Uses AR with “memory palace” to help you remember/memorize a random set of facts. Only have to experience this once to remember a totally random set of facts for up to a year because it becomes associated in the brain with the physical landmarks
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.6958zfck27o0">
 <span class="c18">
  Supporting Mood and Well-being
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Uses EEG to note the brain waves and a wristband to pick up heart rate/galvanic, releases a pleasant smell when it senses anxiety, sharp sense when you’re not focusing enough to wake up and pay attention
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  PsyhicVR: Uses EEG headband to notice brain activity in combination of VR: as long as the brain is concentrated and focused, can make things levitate or other crazy things
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.vzcna1tmogxp">
 <span class="c18">
  “We are cyborgs, and forever will be cyborgs”
 </span>
</h3>
<hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
<h1 class="c10 c24 c50" id="h.dej6yzgtj2vx">
 <span class="c13">
 </span>
</h1>
<h1 class="c10 c24" id="h.x0rh5t9gsgld">
 <span class="c13">
  Augmented Reality
 </span>
</h1>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Augmented reality refers to any augmentation of our natural senses
 </span>
 <sup>
  <a href="#ftnt2" id="ftnt_ref2">
   [2]
  </a>
 </sup>
 <span>
  . Augmented reality encompases traditional experiences like those provided in smartphones today
 </span>
 <sup>
  <a href="#ftnt3" id="ftnt_ref3">
   [3]
  </a>
 </sup>
 <span class="c2">
  . It also includes experiences delivered in fully-immersive Virtual Reality experiences. We can represent AR on a spectrum from the real world to that of the virtual:
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 619.64px; height: 196.50px;">
  <img alt="" src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 619.64px; height: 196.50px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""/>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Figure:
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/ZNyK&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479624000">
   [Milgram et al. 1995]
  </a>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  On this particular spectrum exist two primary stages of manipulation:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_4gk5gp4evkaf-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Augmented reality
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Virtual reality
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  A second, more useful spectrum exists on the scale of VR to AR. “True AR” encompasses a system “[fused coherently] with the user’s real environment.”
 </span>
 <span>
  In traditional formulations of AR, AR forms a proper superset of VR where in VR “we just need to block the user’s experience of the real world.”
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/8tj6&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479624000">
   [Sandor et al. 2015]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span>
  Thus, as VR substitutes the entire visual experience, it demands a higher-level of realism than AR.
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/8tj6&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479625000">
   [Sandor et al. 2015]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  segment their approaches to AR into four categories ranging from “manipulating atoms” to “manipulating perception”:
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_f70w6aek6q9a-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Controlled Matter
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Surround AR
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Personalized AR
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Implanted AR
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.m6lflxz8q6rd">
 <span>
  The Reality-Virtuality
 </span>
 <span class="c1">
  Spectrum
 </span>
</h2>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  There is quite a bit of marketing language from head-worn display manufacturers that occludes a simple understanding of this subject.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.aabs6e8pinut">
 <span class="c18">
  Real environment
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Simple enough to grasp, this is the real world in which we all reside and perceive.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.lr4q647gjy2p">
 <span class="c18">
  Augmented reality (AR)
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  This form of augmentation encompasses a broader scope of marketing terms including divided into two broad categories:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_ogedt8i8kpwv-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   those involving registered graphics and
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   those involving static graphics.
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  It’s important to note that both static and registered graphics can still make use of contextual information
 </span>
 <sup>
  <a href="#ftnt4" id="ftnt_ref4">
   [4]
  </a>
 </sup>
 <span class="c2">
  in similar ways; only the mechanism of conveying such information is different between these forms of AR.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.drhp06r4i8lg">
 <span class="c16">
  Registered graphics
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c28">
  Registered graphics
 </span>
 <span>
  encompasses technologies developed by Microsoft (“Mixed Reality”) or augmented reality solutions developed in the research literature (e.g. Starner, Feiner, et. al) known as
 </span>
 <span class="c28">
  registered AR
 </span>
 <span>
  or
 </span>
 <span class="c28">
  spatial AR
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  .
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  This form of AR involves placing virtual computer artifacts into the real world by either:
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_epefovixow43-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   displaying such graphics through a traditional display (i.e. an iPhone running ARKit), or
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span>
   displaying such graphics through a holographic display (i.e. a HoloLens).
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 616.50px; height: 413.85px;">
  <img alt="" src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 616.50px; height: 413.85px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""/>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  A holographic display placing registered graphics into the real world. Figure:
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/L36u&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479628000">
   [Buntz]
  </a>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.dik69v264z8m">
 <span class="c16">
  Static graphics
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Depending on the use case, static graphics may be more applicable. This form involves displaying static information generated by a computer that
 </span>
 <span class="c25">
  does not
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  include an image of the real environment.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.b4wxhm4ta6n">
 <span class="c18">
  Virtual Reality
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c0 c24" id="h.5klnf53tos7d">
 <span class="c18">
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Virtual reality (VR) involves complete immersion in a virtual environment with little or none of the real environment available to the user.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 624.00px; height: 289.33px;">
  <img alt="" src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 624.00px; height: 289.33px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""/>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Figure:
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/KjLj&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479629000">
   [[CSL STYLE ERROR: reference with no printed form.]]
  </a>
 </span>
 <hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
</p>
<h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.sgbu9gfhz306">
 <span>
  Augmented Reality Spectrum
 </span>
</h2>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  This spectrum exists on a different axis from the Reality-Virtuality Spectrum and discusses the theoretical mechanisms with which reality can be manipulated.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.sna0tkf7s9f2">
 <span class="c18">
  Controlled Matter
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 620.50px; height: 467.87px;">
  <img alt="" src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 620.50px; height: 467.87px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""/>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Figure:
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/KEbv&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479631000">
   [Zambetta 2017]
  </a>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Think The HoloDeck from
 </span>
 <span class="c25">
  Star Trek
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  : matter is created and destroyed, or at the minimum photons are controlled by ‘force fields’ giving the impression of physical objects and interactions.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Another, more tangible
 </span>
 <sup>
  <a href="#ftnt5" id="ftnt_ref5">
   [5]
  </a>
 </sup>
 <span>
  , example is the
 </span>
 <span class="c43">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://tangible.media.mit.edu/project/inform/&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479631000">
   inFORM project
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  from MIT Media Lab:
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 624.00px; height: 416.00px;">
  <img alt="" src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 624.00px; height: 416.00px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""/>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  Figure:
 </span>
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/HJKN&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479632000">
   [2013]
  </a>
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c6">
  <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/8tj6&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479632000">
   [Sandor et al. 2015]
  </a>
 </span>
 <span class="c2">
  notes Sutherland’s suggestion that physically creating and destroying atoms forms an ideal for True AR because it would “create physical objects consistent over all interaction modalities and all users.”
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.4i9ctd822rh3">
 <span class="c18">
  Surround AR
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  The next level closer to the user is by “manipulating [the] photons” that reach them. Surround AR lacks the physical interactivity enabled by Controlled Matter but can create an augmented reality indistinguishable from physical reality.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Think of an empty room panelled with high-fidelity displays. As the user walks around, her entire perception of the room changes. You can simulate what it’s like to stand in Wrigley Field: as your head moves around the room, the environment tracks you, and updates the environment accordingly to provide the illusion of movement.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  However, if you were at Wrigley Field, you couldn’t sit down at the bleeachers and enjoy a hot dog. Matter itself isn’t manipulated, only light.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.dj0h31ibmuu8">
 <span class="c18">
  Personalized AR
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  HWDs like Google Glass or Magic Leap provide us with this level of augmentation. Our visual field is augmented with new objects placed indistinguishably from the physical world. Each user augments their own visual perception. This doesn’t preclude shared experiences but requires some level high-speed networking.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.qx8dbkkz4dj3">
 <span class="c18">
  Implant AR
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Completely invisible to the outside world, this level of AR involves directly manipulating where visual perception is interpreted: in our brains. An implant is placed in or near the visual cortex and directly manipulates our perception of the physical world.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Think controlled LSD trip.
 </span>
</p>
<hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h1 class="c10 c24" id="h.iapjfz8gi90d">
 <span class="c13">
  The Design of Head-Worn Displays
 </span>
</h1>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Currently, HWDs form the highest-bandwidth bridge to convey information to the brain. Although implant or surface-worn BCIs could theoretically form the ideal way to convey information to and from the brain, current limitations on bandwidth make HWDs a better option.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  In this section, we detail various aspects of the design of HWDs.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  There are a few broad categories of use
 </span>
</p>
<ol class="c23 lst-kix_ssadkqniom3o-0 start" start="1">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Consumer every-day
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Consumer gaming
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Industrial
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Medical
  </span>
 </li>
</ol>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Each of which requires a call upon different balances of the dimensions of design.
 </span>
</p>
<hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.1bx598vtxbkx">
 <span class="c1">
  Dimensions of design
 </span>
</h2>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.wd6tn6ia5zm1">
 <span class="c18">
  Age-related issues
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c0 c24" id="h.jnmkyc945yr3">
 <span class="c18">
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.4yspfnteedhm">
 <span class="c18">
  Audio
 </span>
</h3>
<h4 class="c7 c29" id="h.xh7hr06tf3g5">
 <span class="c16">
 </span>
</h4>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.r2ao1wam96or">
 <span class="c16">
  Brain-Conducting Transmission
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.w8fbby9cy25j">
 <span class="c18">
  Battery &amp; Charging
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.7jqe3r90886b">
 <span class="c18">
  Controllers &amp; Sensors
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.rwpurlww58lt">
 <span class="c16">
  Wired vs. all on head
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.2inpecic4ea0">
 <span class="c16">
  CPU
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.aoaogc61frft">
 <span class="c16">
  GPU
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.bgwqavysyd5s">
 <span class="c16">
  Sensors vs. not having sensors
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.3kxa3yu4lluf">
 <span class="c16">
  Available sensors
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<ul class="c23 lst-kix_xt4qsv5tpojw-0 start">
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Acceleratormeter
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Compass
  </span>
 </li>
 <li class="c8">
  <span class="c2">
   Gyroscope
  </span>
 </li>
</ul>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.k59yabkmv390">
 <span class="c16">
  Sensor fusion
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.sh62ggnsl3mm">
 <span class="c18">
  Registered vs. Static AR
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c0 c24" id="h.i0pbide5yl48">
 <span class="c18">
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.5ckdo57t6c9i">
 <span class="c18">
  Human Visual Perception
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.rs0pyl6m5i8f">
 <span class="c16">
  Vergence vs. Accommodation
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.kblld7dqli5w">
 <span class="c18">
  Fashion: Xybernaut vs. Glass vs. North
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.vmvqn3dy8a8f">
 <span class="c18">
  Human Factors
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.gt6628v62l7">
 <span class="c16">
  Sweat &amp; Nose Pads
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.x2ehcjmered0">
 <span class="c16">
  Hair
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.33h8vc1l8gir">
 <span class="c16">
  Don / doff: Taking it on and off
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.65ca1yxfrjd2">
 <span class="c16">
  Fit:  “No one is average”
 </span>
</h4>
<h4 class="c7 c29" id="h.z3mpxcsybdaz">
 <span class="c16">
 </span>
</h4>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.ol9retrelwnz">
 <span class="c16">
  Ego motion / nausea
 </span>
</h4>
<h3 class="c0 c24" id="h.wugljzvl2get">
 <span class="c18">
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.eea8zannbigq">
 <span class="c18">
  Optics &amp; Display
 </span>
</h3>
<h4 class="c7 c29" id="h.io1ivtiw12dp">
 <span class="c16">
 </span>
</h4>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.1chzbws6xi4z">
 <span class="c16">
  Flat focus
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.5pkd552cou4">
 <span class="c16">
  Field-of-view
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.e46v4fw5p7cz">
 <span class="c16">
  Field-of-regard
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.4j4u68wimyyd">
 <span class="c16">
  Monocular vs. Binocular
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.hb2uu7euyuiv">
 <span class="c16">
  Eyebox: Binoculars, Vignetting
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.jp409jja7zs9">
 <span class="c16">
  Color
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.h1teq57kwc5k">
 <span class="c16">
  Resolution
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.vwr2fmuc1yl6">
 <span class="c16">
  Movement while in use
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.dbev3qypcaz3">
 <span class="c16">
  Focal depth: static vs. fixed, multiplane (like MagicLeap)
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.7mun6vkjat1b">
 <span class="c16">
  Night vision
 </span>
</h4>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h4 class="c7" id="h.uc0ua9fsqhll">
 <span class="c16">
  Positioning:

<h2 class="c10 c24 c45" id="h.u36rf2wkzen">

<h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.mjm49hja0l5h">
 <span class="c1">
  Categories of use
 </span>

<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.l9puunoos1t5">
 <span class="c18">
  Consumer, every-day
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span class="c2">
  Everyday consumer-wearable head-worn displays are exciting because of symbiosis between humans and machines enabled by their constant usage: Data captured and inputted into the device can build larger and larger datasets that can be analyzed and made useful to the user.
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>

  Professional gaming
 </span>

  Industrial
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c0 c24" id="h.1azultxjv4je">
 <span class="c18">
 </span>
</h3>
<h3 class="c10 c24" id="h.a0jc4ksf1vml">
 <span class="c18">
  Medical
 </span>
</h3>
<p class="c0">
 <span class="c2">
 </span>
</p>
<p class="c10">
 <span>
  In medical applications, privacy is of utmost concern requiring careful attention to the software and hardware usage of voice and camera input. Computer networking and offsite APIs will need to be carefully designed to be compliant with relevant regulations like HIPAA.
 </span>
 <hr style="page-break-before:always;display:none;"/>
</p>

<h2 class="c10 c24 c45" id="h.q66krdq92fx6">
 <span class="c1">
 </span>
</h2>
<a id="t.a9384331e65956a3aa6960a4a59126c857d4419e">
</a>
<a id="t.2">
</a>
<table class="c4">
 <tbody>
  <tr class="c14">
   <td class="c51" colspan="1" rowspan="1">
    <h2 class="c10 c24" id="h.85wmbjnesurg">
     <span class="c1">
      Pattie Maes TED Talk: Human-Machine Symbiosis
     </span>
    </h2>
    <p class="c0">
     <span class="c2">
     </span>
    </p>
    <p class="c10">
     <span>
      Source:
     </span>
     <span class="c6">
      <a class="c3" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://paperpile.com/c/mpEskP/se69&amp;sa=D&amp;ust=1588900479654000">
       [Maes 1997]
      </a>
     </span>
    </p>
    <p class="c0">
     <span class="c2">
     </span>
    </p>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-0 start" start="1">
     <li class="c8">
      <span class="c2">
       We become cyborgs: kids get a smartphone at age 12-14
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1 start" start="1">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       The two halves of our brains have become the biological and digital
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2 start" start="1">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Increasingly, we rely on our digital brain to answer questions when we are asked something rather than using our biological brain to come up with a solution.
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       The two halves of our brain don’t talk well together:
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ul class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-3 start">
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Communication is limited: limited I/O bandwidth
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Requires our complete attention, disengaging us from the real world.
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       The software hasn’t been designed with the goals of people in mind. Different apps on phone are trying to distract you as much as possible, making you as inefficient and ineffective at accomplishing goals -&gt; multitasking, short attention spans
      </span>
     </li>
    </ul>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-0" start="2">
     <li class="c8">
      <span class="c2">
       Pattie Maes: It is our destintiny to augment ourselves with whatever tools and technologies, and merge with technology itself
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1 start" start="1">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       We will become one with the computer, but we must redesign the experience of how someone interacts with their digital devices.
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Argues for a new approach:
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2 start" start="1">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       System aware of context &amp; user
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ul class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-3 start">
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Aware of context and user’s internal state, what the user is paying attention to, brain activity, heart rate, breathing rate, etc.
      </span>
     </li>
    </ul>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2" start="2">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Always-on augmented interface
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ul class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-3 start">
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Seamless, non-disruptive way
      </span>
     </li>
    </ul>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2" start="3">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Proactive, personalized interaction
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ul class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-3 start">
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Offer relevant information and intervention, given what the user is currently trying to do, the user’s state, and the user’s goal
      </span>
     </li>
    </ul>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-0" start="3">
     <li class="c8">
      <span class="c2">
       Prior work: on-body camera and projector
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1 start" start="1">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Experience is synergistic and incorporated
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Experience the physical environment and benefiting from digital information
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-0" start="4">
     <li class="c8">
      <span class="c2">
       Symbiotic relationship between users and machines will help with self-actualization, with growing and developing into the people we want to become.
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1 start" start="1">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       We all want to change and grow in different ways.
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       We will rely on symbiotic forms of personal devices more and more to help us change with time
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-0" start="5">
     <li class="c8">
      <span class="c2">
       Symbiotic devices will change the way we make decisions, learn, remember, and regulate our mood
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1 start" start="1">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Supporting Decision Making
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2 start" start="1">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Up to 90% of the decisions we make are a result of natural thinking that may not be in\line with our goals
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1" start="2">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Support Learning
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2 start" start="1">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Using AR to label objects in the real world (WordSense)
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ul class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-3 start">
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Can give you new words for known objects, etc.
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c32">
      <span class="c2">
       Not all of the devices need to rely on a smart AI system
      </span>
     </li>
    </ul>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2" start="2">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Google Glass in a supermarket for learning a new language through a “remote assistant” system
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       AR for “remote assistant”
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1" start="3">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Supporting Memory
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2 start" start="1">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Shaking hand to remember someone’s name and face (TakeTwo)
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Uses AR with “memory palace” to help you remember/memorize a random set of facts. Only have to experience this once to remember a totally random set of facts for up to a year because it becomes associated in the brain with the physical landmarks
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-1" start="4">
     <li class="c5">
      <span class="c2">
       Supporting Mood and Well-being
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-2 start" start="1">
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       Uses EEG to note the brain waves and a wristband to pick up heart rate/galvanic, releases a pleasant smell when it senses anxiety, sharp sense when you’re not focusing enough to wake up and pay attention
      </span>
     </li>
     <li class="c10 c27">
      <span class="c2">
       PsyhicVR: Uses EEG headband to notice brain activity in combination of VR: as long as the brain is concentrated and focused, can make things levitate or other crazy things
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <ol class="c23 lst-kix_9pvywtok2q2y-0" start="6">
     <li class="c8">
      <span class="c2">
       “Let’s embrace our cyborg future but redesign our devices to a natural extension that assists and empowers”
      </span>
     </li>
    </ol>
    <p class="c10">
     <span>
      “We are cyborgs, and forever will be cyborgs”
     </span>
    </p>
   </td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>
